findings.evidence: Sidebar at state 04 contains data-testid="kiosk-categories-sidebar-item-306" (Tacos), data-testid="kiosk-categories-sidebar-item-307" (Sandwichs), data-testid="kiosk-categories-sidebar-item-308" (Burgers) — exact DOM grep on 04-categories-welcome.dom.html confirms all three. The owner gate (AUDIT_PLAN.md line 7 + line 26 + line 235) explicitly states 'Cats 306 / 307 / 308 (sandwich / burger / tacos) — owner gate' OUT OF SCOPE / hidden. Source resources/js/store/modules/kioskMenu.js:78 only filters cat 315: `KIOSK_HIDDEN_CATEGORY_IDS = new Set([315])`. Customer can navigate to and ADD products from these categories that the owner has explicitly excluded — the kiosk will accept the cart, send to KDS, and charge for products outside the owner's intended catalog. This is a silent revenue leak / unauthorized sale risk. Verified across all 9 cat-browse states (05–13): every screenshot shows TACOS / SANDWICHS / BURGERS persistently in the sidebar.
findings.fix_hint: resources/js/store/modules/kioskMenu.js:78 — extend `KIOSK_HIDDEN_CATEGORY_IDS = new Set([315])` to `new Set([306, 307, 308, 315])`. Alternatively introduce a server-side branch-config flag (kiosk_hidden_categories) seeded from settings table so owners can manage the exclusion without code change. Add Vitest regression: tests/js/kioskMenu.spec.js asserting categories 306/307/308 absent from `selectableCategories` getter.

findings.evidence: DOM grep `data-testid="kiosk-categories-sidebar-item-307"` returns 2 occurrences in 04-categories-welcome.dom.html with two distinct `kiosk-sidebar-name` labels: 'Sandwichs' and 'Sandwich froid'. findings.fix_hint: resources/js/helpers/kioskSandwichSplit.js — assign distinct data-testid to the cold-sandwich virtual row (e.g. `kiosk-categories-sidebar-item-307-cold` or `kiosk-categories-sidebar-item-307-virtual`). findings.evidence: DOM grep on 04-categories-welcome.dom.html finds the rejected pink hex `#E8001C` 11 times in inline styles, plus its rgb form `232, 0, 28` 18 times and `232,0,28` 4 times — a total of 33 instances of the legacy pink palette in the rendered page. The Cayenne primary `#F4501E` (244,80,30) is also present (22 hex + 13 rgb), so the page mixes both palettes simultaneously. The audit-plan acceptance criterion (Wave A line 46) explicitly requires `Cayenne primary #F4501E not pink #E8001C`. The spec's pink_present check (L211) returns false because it inspects only `[data-testid="kiosk-categories-pay"]` background-image, but pink is leaking elsewhere on the page (likely via FoodKing logo SVG/text and other inline-styled elements). The PNG of state 01–03 visually confirms the pink FoodKing wordmark on the idle screen — the brand logo itself is rendered in pink #E8001C, not Cayenne #F4501E, in violation of the owner palette gate.
findings.fix_hint: Locate inline style/CSS-var sources of #E8001C across kiosk components: grep -r '#E8001C\|232, 0, 28' resources/js resources/css public/css. Likely candidates: KioskHeader logo, kiosk-theme tokens. Replace all with Cayenne `#F4501E` per docs/branding. Audit-plan claim that pink is absent from the pay button is technically true but misses the larger surface — the spec's color check is too narrow and misses the brand logo + secondary surfaces.

findings.evidence: Cat 318 'Suppléments' grid: DOM has 8 product cards but 8 of them use `src="/storage/<n>/item-default.svg"` placeholder (grep `item-default.svg` returned 8 matches in 13-cat-318-supplements.dom.html). (2) UX — when no image exists, the placeholder should at minimum show a category-icon glyph or a descriptive skeleton, not the same generic '+'. resources/js/components/frontend/kiosk/KioskProductCardComponent.vue (or equivalent) — fall back to a category emoji + label background when item.image_url is item-default.svg.

findings.evidence: On state 04 (welcome / first paint after takeaway tap), the right-side product grid auto-displays cat 317 BOISSONS (8 boisson cards rendered immediately — verified by grep `kiosk-product-card-` count = 8 in 04-categories-welcome.dom.html and the PNG showing the BOISSONS title). findings.evidence: Across all cat-browse states (05–13) the right-rail green '+' add-to-cart button appears in every product card. DOM grep on a product card shows the button uses an icon-only render (the visible '+' glyph). Each card has data-testid `kiosk-product-card-<id>` but the inner add button needs aria-label='Ajouter <product name> au panier' for screen-reader users; without it the user hears 'button' or 'plus' with no product context. Need to verify on the actual button element (could not exhaustively inspect every product card markup in this round; flagging for round 2 to verify).
findings.fix_hint: Check resources/js/components/frontend/kiosk/KioskProductCardComponent.vue or equivalent — the '+' icon button should have aria-label binding to product name. Pattern: `<button :aria-label="$t('kiosk.add_product_to_cart', { name: product.name })">`. Verify the i18n key resolves to a usable string in fr.json kiosk namespace.

findings.evidence: GStack agent claim 'Cayenne palette sentinel: getComputedStyle on pay-button bg-image returned a non-matching string for 244,80,30' — assertion was made specifically on `[data-testid="kiosk-categories-pay"]`. Inspecting that element via DOM grep on 04-categories-welcome.dom.html: the pay button container has class `kiosk-pay-cta` but the inner styles reference background gradients with both #F4501E (Cayenne) AND #E8001C (pink) in the same DOM. Reviewer cannot conclude whether the rendered pay button is Cayenne or pink without a live page paint, so the spec's narrow check is insufficient evidence. Coupled with finding A-003/A-005, the page-wide palette is mixed. The GStack claim that the palette is OK is at best unverified and at worst false. The spec test passed because pinkPresent regex did not match within the 400-char serialized palette substring (L210), but the 400-char clip is not exhaustive — many palette references live in CSS classes outside that slice.
findings.fix_hint: Spec line 198–211 — replace the 400-char string-clip + regex check with: (a) a full computedStyle.backgroundImage extraction (no slice), (b) a dedicated DOM-wide audit grepping all rendered elements' computed background colors, (c) a deterministic CSS-var inspection: `getComputedStyle(:root).getPropertyValue('--kiosk-primary')` should equal `#F4501E`. Round 2 must add a pixel-level visual diff against a known-good Cayenne baseline as well.

notes: Wave A round 1 — 13 states reviewed with quartet (PNG/DOM/console/network) per state. Two P0 findings dominate: A-001 (cats 306/307/308 visible despite owner gate — silent revenue leak) and A-012 (palette assertion narrow scope leaves Cayenne sentinel unproven). Three P1 findings on palette drift (A-003 33 instances of pink #E8001C in the welcome DOM, A-005 brand logo pink, A-002 duplicate testid for cat 307). The kioskMenu.js source code at line 78 confirms the filter is `new Set([315])` ONLY — the owner gate for 306/307/308 is NOT enforced. Round 2 must (a) extend KIOSK_HIDDEN_CATEGORY_IDS to include 306/307/308, (b) eliminate ALL #E8001C from kiosk surfaces, (c) fix duplicate-testid cat-307-split, (d) tighten the palette spec assertion to be DOM-wide rather than 400-char slice, (e) decide on language-selector scope (drop states 02/03 OR fix the env). DO NOT declare green until open_P0 == 0 AND open_P1 == 0. Allowlisted: WebSocket Pusher dev-mode errors (A-007 P3 info only).
